extracted.intended_audience: war correspondents, press agencies, and general newspaper readers
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and health/supply guidance for newspaper correspondents assigned or volunteering for overseas war coverage: required immunizations, equipment, nomination/approval rules, and operational precautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: War Department immunization requirements for correspondents
rubrics_metrics.description: By official order those who follow the 300-odd Americans who have gone abroad since Pearl Harbor to cover the fighting fronts may take as many as seven 'shots in the arm' as safeguards against germs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance immunization called for smallpox, typhoid and paratyphoid and tetanus. Smallpox vaccination involves one operation; the three typhoid injections require about two weeks to complete; immunization against tetanus is a six-week process. Additional special immunizations will be required for correspondents who will be stationed in or travel through areas where particular maladies are endemic. The inoculation order emphasizes that vaccinations should, under ordinary circumstances, be completed before the correspondent is provided with transportation abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disease-specific endemic-risk guidance for overseas travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain diseases are identified as endemic to particular world regions and therefore require specific immunization considerations for travelers and correspondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typhus: considered endemic to all Europe, Asia, Africa, the East Indies, Central America and much of South America (i.e., most regions outside North America, Greenland, Iceland, Australasia and parts of South America indicated). Cholera: considered endemic to all of Asia and the East Indies. Yellow fever: considered endemic to Central Africa and the northern section of South America from the southerly point of Brazil. Special immunizations should be given when travel is to areas where these maladies are peculiar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination, vetting and approval process for overseas correspondents
rubrics_metrics.description: An overseas-bound correspondent must be nominated by his press agency and is subject to special investigation before being approved by the War or Navy Departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The correspondent is 'nominated by his press agency,' undergoes 'special investigation' and must be approved by the War or Navy Departments. Like officers, correspondents are required to provide their own uniform and equipment and are subject to searches and security vetting. Approval is contingent on meeting health (inoculation) and security requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required/ recommended personal equipment for overseas correspondents
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Department provided a suggested list of basic equipment items for correspondents assigned overseas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested items include: garrison and overseas caps; two pairs dark uniform trousers; dark uniform blouse; two officer-type wool shirts; two khaki cotton shirts; two pairs of high tan shoes; one pair canvas leggings; a raincoat; regulation foot locker; overshoes/galoshes; underwear and socks; a musette bag; bedding roll; barracks coat; cotton uniforms according to climate at destination. The page notes correspondents usually must provide their own uniform and equipment, typically costing more than $200 for a minimum outfit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational/security conditions for assignment (correspondent movement and disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondents assigned to certain operations may be transported or embarked without being told their destination and may be restricted from telling others they are leaving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A correspondent may be given the opportunity to accompany a task force or expedition 'without being told destination or permitted to tell others he is leaving.' Overseas travel can last weeks; correspondents are subject to searching and other security measures while en route and on assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legion of Merit award criteria (military decoration guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new military decoration (the Legion of Merit) will recognize 'extraordinary fidelity and essential service' in a position of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Legion of Merit is intended for 'extraordinary fidelity and essential service' in positions of responsibility and is not given for gallantry in action. It takes precedence below the Distinguished Service Medal and above awards given for wounds; heroism in combat continues to be recognized by awards such as the Medal of Honor, Distinguished Service Cross and Silver Star. The medal's basic appearance and ribbon colors are described (red-and-white enamel star, purple-red ribbon edged with white).
